messages:
rachel.devex: heads up  onboarding reported a confusing notebook cell in samples/notebooks/embeddings/README.ipynb. the example shows using `client.embed()` (openai-like) and indexing into `resp['embeddings'][0]`, but our python SDK v1.4 shape is `client.embeddings.create(input=...)` returning `{'data': [{'embedding': [...]}, ...]}`. kevin.newhire hit a KeyError and lost ~25 minutes this morning.

kevin.newhire: paste of the cell I ran (copy/paste from notebook):

```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
resp = client.embed(["hello world"])  # README example
print(resp['embeddings'][0])
```

kevin.newhire: error I got: `KeyError: 'embeddings'` and then I saw `AttributeError: module 'redwood' has no attribute 'Client'` because my installed package was different from the snippet. super confusing.

tony.engineer: thanks for the repro. two drift factors: 1) notebook was edited to show a conceptual openai-style example but never updated to our SDK shape, 2) samples/requirements.txt pins `redwood-sdk==0.9.2` while onboarding images and our docs reference v1.4. so copy/paste + pinned deps mismatch.

sasha.docs: ok. proposed fixed notebook cell (Python SDK v1.4+):

```python
from redwood.client import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
resp = client.embeddings.create(input=["hello world"])  # SDK v1.4 shape
# resp = {'data': [{'embedding': [...]}], 'model': 'redwood-embed'}
embedding = resp['data'][0]['embedding']
print(len(embedding))
```

kevin.newhire: that works locally with the newer wheel. thank you! adding the exact error text to the notebook would have helped me find this faster.

rachel.devex: let's do three changes: 1) update the notebook cell to the new snippet, 2) bump samples/requirements.txt to `redwood-sdk>=1.4.0`, 3) add a short "Notebook gotchas" markdown cell showing the old snippet + the exact KeyError / AttributeError so search can surface it for support.

tony.engineer: also propose adding a tiny CI job that runs `nbconvert --execute` (headless) on that notebook against a local SDK stub which mirrors the v1.4 return shape. that will catch future copy/paste drifts where docs are updated but examples not executed. cheap and quick.

sasha.docs: +1 on CI. i'll open PR with the notebook update, requirements bump, a short migration note in samples/CHANGES.md, and a GH Action `notebook-smoke` that runs nbconvert with a stubbed `redwood` package available in the job. will include the error messages in the notebook under "Common mistakes".

notebook-bot: PR #1182 created by sasha.docs  running notebook-smoke. :gear:

kevin.newhire: small UX nit  the notebook currently hides stack traces in output cells which made the original error hard to copy. can we ensure the notebook keeps full errors when executed in CI so new hires can copy-paste them into support threads?

rachel.devex: good point. sasha, can you leave the raw traceback in an output cell (commented) so it appears in the rendered notebook and is visible in GitHub? makes triage easier.

sasha.docs: will do. adding the full traceback output and a short troubleshooting note. merging once CI green.

tony.engineer: once merged, i'll also update the onboarding checklist to note "run notebook-smoke locally when editing notebooks" so maintainers remember to execute examples. small change but big onboarding ROI.

notebook-bot: PR #1182 CI passed  notebook-smoke succeeded. :white_check_mark:

sasha.docs: merged and released sample v0.9.0. posted migration note in #onboarding and added the error text to docs search. thanks for the quick turnaround.

rachel.devex: nice work team. notebooks are extremely helpful but fragile; executing them in CI and surfacing the exact errors saves devs a lot of time. :sparkles:
